sources.citation: Carrington, John F. 1949. A comparative study of some Central African gong-languages. (Memoires IRCB, Sciences morales et politiques, XVIII-3.) Brussels: IRCB.
sources.note: Contains Mbole (D11) gong-language texts from four areas (Botunga, Bolinga, Yaamba, Yalikoka), pp. 96-103, but no Mbole-specific prosodic statement. The only prominence statement is general, p.45: 'In Kele and some surrounding languages the most prominent syllable in the spoken language is the penultimate, irrespective of the grammatical nature of this syllable' -- Mbole is not named, so this cannot be booked as a Mbole statement.

sources.citation: Hulstaert, Gustaaf. 1988. Le parler des Lokalo orientaux. Annales Aequatoria 9: 133-171.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Nothing. Section I 'Phonemes' (p.135) treats only vowels and consonant sequences; the introduction (p.134) states the data carry no tone marks at all ('Pour moi l'inconvenient majeur est l'absence totale de signes pour la tonologie'). NB identity: this is Hulstaert's Mongo dialect no. 187 (Lokalo of Bokungu/Yotuna/Yasakanga, Ikela zone, Equateur), a Mongo/C61 variety, not D11 Mbole of Opala; Glottolog's assignment to mbol1247 looks like a name-based misassignment.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, Andre. 2009. Le reseau fluvial congolais et la problematique de l'expansion bantoue. Annales Aequatoria 30: 839-988.
sources.note: Nothing on Mbole stress. Cites de Rop 1971 as the description of 'mbɔlɛ D11' (vocalic noun prefixes cl.1,2,3,4,6; progressive forms p.66; locative preposition pp.73-74); its comparative section 3.2.2 'Tonologie' discusses pausal low tone and tone cases in other languages only.

tone.quote: Il existe phonétiquement trois tons en liinja: haut, moyen et bas. Ce dernier ton est marqué par l’absence de tout signe diacritique. [...] Ainsi que l’indiquent ces exemples (41), le ton moyen est le réhaussement d’un ton bas dans une séquence °H-B en fin d’énoncé ou dans les unités de citation. [...] Comme notre transcription est phonétique, nous marquons tout de même le ton moyen là où nous l’avons perçu, bien que phonologiquement il n’existe que le ton bas et le ton haut. [...] Les principales règles tonales sont: la fusion, la propagation, la neutralisation et l’harmonie. A celles-ci s’ajoute le morphème tonal.
tone.locator: pp. 297-298, section 2.3.1 'Inventaire des tons' and opening of 2.3.2 'Règles tonales'
tone.translation: Phonetically there are three tones in Liinja: high, mid and low. The low tone is marked by the absence of any diacritic. [...] As these examples (41) show, the mid tone is the raising of a low tone in an underlying H-L sequence at the end of an utterance or in citation units. [...] Since our transcription is phonetic we nevertheless mark the mid tone where we perceived it, although phonologically only the low tone and the high tone exist. [...] The main tone rules are fusion, spreading, neutralisation and harmony; to these is added the tonal morpheme.
tone.summary: 2 level tones H vs L (lexical and grammatical contrasts); phonetic mid = raised L after H utterance-finally; downstep; rules: contraction fusion, spreading, H plateau/bridge, affixal tone harmony, replacive grammatical tone in verb forms; no stress/accent discussed.

sources.note: The only published grammar sketch of D11 Mbole (WALS's source; cited by Motingea 2009 for D11). A Mongo-school sketch by de Rop will have a 'Tons'/'Phonologie' section and may state whether there is a dynamic accent (Hulstaert-school sketches usually note 'accent dynamique' on the stem-initial syllable or its absence).
